1.

Perusal of the record would reveal that as per communication sent by the Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Balrampur of date 05.08.2023, opposite party no.2 has been sufficiently/personally
served and she is also represented by Shri Raziuddin Ahmad Siddiqui, however, he (Shri Raziuddin
Ahmad Siddiqui) is neither present nor any request has been made on his behalf to adjourn the case.

2. Heard Shri Mohd. Waris Farooqui, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Mohammad Kaleem for grant of bail, in Case Crime No.145 of 2023, under Sections 363, 376, 506 I.P.C. read with Section 3/4 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act, Police Station Rehra Bazar, District Balrampur, during trial.

sentences.text: 5. It is further submitted that F.I.R. of this case has been lodged by the mother of the prosecutrix on 20.05.2023 at Police Station Rehra Bazar, Balrampur against the applicant and his family members alleging therein that on 17.05.2023 at about 10:00pm.

the applicant had enticed away her daughter aged about 17 years and after keeping her for three days at some unknown place brought her to his house on 19.05.2023 and when she (informant) had gone to meet her daughter she started weeping and she brought her back to her home.
Date of birth of the prosecutrix is stated as 01.01.2006.

Statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., wherein she stated to be in love with the applicant and has stated her age as 21 years and had categorically stated that for the last one year she was talking to the applicant and on 17.05.2023 at about 10:00pm., she had accompanied him on his motorcycle and she was taken to an unknown place, where sexual relations were established between them.

The prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has not imputed any kind of allegations against the applicant and has admitted to have accompanied the applicant with her free wish and consent and also that sexual relations were established between them with her consent and as she was though not major but was of 17 years and 4 months of age (on the basis of her educational credentials) at the date and time of the alleged incident and was having sufficient intellect to understand her welfare and nature of the sexual activity and therefore, no offence has been committed by the applicant.

6. It is next submitted that applicant is in jail in this case since 21.05.2023 and criminal history of two cases is being alleged against the applicant, however, one case is pertaining to Section 498A I.P.C., which is with regard to the matrimonial strained relations of the applicant with his wife and the second case, wherein the prosecutrix of the incident was informant, Final Report/Closure Report has been filed.
Charge-sheet in this case has already been submitted and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail the applicant may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

7. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and having regard to the material/evidence available against the applicant, he is not entitled to be released on bail, but could not controvert the other factual submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant.

8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that as per educational credentials of the prosecutrix, her age was about 17 years and 4 months at the date and time of the alleged incident.
In her medical report, no abnormality or injury of any kind has been noticed.
In her statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., she has not imputed any allegation against the applicant.
Criminal history of two cases has been adequately explained.
Charge-sheet in this case has already been filed.
Applicant is in jail in this case since 21.05.2023.
The presence of the applicant could be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

9. Having regard to the overall facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned Mohammad Kaleem vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55702295/

sentences.text: 2 counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

10. Let the accused/applicant- Mohammad Kaleem involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
11. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
12. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
13. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression of this Court on the merits of the case.
